section_coverage.unit: Chapter 1 §1.1 Probability spaces and measure extension
section_coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: Read σ-fields, countable additivity, continuity of measures, Stieltjes laws and semialgebra/algebra extension. The text states the extension theorem and moves the longer Carathéodory proof to Appendix A.1.
Read push-forward law/CDF properties and inverse-transform construction; measurability is proved by generators, composition, and countable sup/inf limits.
Read the four-stage integral definition, monotone/Fatou/bounded/dominated convergence proofs and Jensen/Hölder. Dominated convergence follows by applying Fatou to f_n+g and −f_n.

Read expectation, inequalities, integration-to-limit including coercive-moment uniform-tail truncation (Theorem 1.6.8), and the change-of-variables identity proved from indicators through simple/nonnegative/general functions.

Read product measure from rectangle values and Fubini via measurable sections, π–λ, simple functions, MCT and positive/negative parts; examples show why absolute integrability and σ-finiteness matter.

Read kernel definition and integral formula, plus existence for the author’s “nice” measurable state spaces: choose a measurable embedding into R, construct conditional CDF versions on a countable rational set, discard a common null set, extend to a distribution function, then use π–λ to obtain all Borel events.

section_coverage.unit: Chapter 4 §4.6 Uniform Integrability, Convergence in L1, including exercises 4.6.1–4.6.7
section_coverage.content_and_proof_mechanism: Read UI definition and tail bound; conditional-expectation UI, de la Vallée–Poussin sufficient condition, Vitali equivalence for convergence in probability, submartingale/martingale convergence, representation X_n=E(X|F_n), and increasing-filtration conditional-expectation convergence. The complete exercise continuation on physical p.257 was also read; exercises 4.6.2–4.6.7 concern Lipschitz-function martingale derivatives/integral representation, L1 step approximation, a hitting-zero/infinity dichotomy, branching-process extinction/infinite growth, Bernoulli martingale endpoints, and conditional-expectation L1 convergence.

Read Theorem 3.2.8 inverse-CDF coupling (exceptional flat intervals are countable), Theorem 3.2.9 bounded-continuous test characterization, Theorem 3.2.10 a.s.-continuous mapping, Theorem 3.2.11 Portmanteau, Helly diagonal selection, and Theorems 3.2.13–3.2.14 separating tightness from mass escape and deriving tightness from a coercive moment bound. The cited representation is the real-line version.

Read Theorem 3.3.17 and its proof: average 1−φ over [−u,u] controls tail mass outside 2/u; continuity at zero makes the bound small, pointwise convergence plus bounded convergence transfers it to μ_n, tightness yields weakly convergent subsubsequences, and characteristic-function uniqueness plus the subsequence principle gives the full limit.

Read Theorem 3.10.1 metric Portmanteau via Lipschitz distance-to-closed-set approximants and range quantization; Theorem 3.10.2 good-rectangle CDF criterion; Theorem 3.10.3 rational-grid diagonal tight subsequence; Theorem 3.10.5 characteristic-function convergence; Theorem 3.10.6 Cramér–Wold; and the finite-second-moment multivariate CLT Theorem 3.10.7. Scope remains R^d.

Read Theorems 4.1.9–4.1.15. Integral characterization proves linearity/order/monotone convergence; conditional Jensen uses a countable rational affine minorant family to manage null sets; Jensen gives Lp contraction; nested sigma-fields give tower identities; pull-out is proved from indicators to integrable products; L2 orthogonality yields the conditional-expectation projection.

Read martingale definitions and examples, iterated conditional inequalities, convex transforms, predictable betting/stopping, the (b−a)E U_n upcrossing bound, and the rational-interval/Fatou proof that sup_n E X_n^+<∞ for a submartingale yields a finite integrable a.s. limit. The nonnegative-supermartingale corollary and counterexamples distinguish a.s. convergence from L1 or probability convergence.

Read all six exercise statements before the §4.7 heading: (4.6.2) Lipschitz dyadic difference quotients form a martingale and recover f(b)-f(a) by integration; (4.6.3) conditional step approximants give L1 step-function density; (4.6.4) a conditional lower bound on eventual hitting-zero yields zero-or-divergence; (4.6.5) apply that dichotomy to branching-process extinction when p0>0; (4.6.6) a [0,1]-valued martingale has endpoint limit with P(limit=1)=X0; (4.6.7) increasing-filtration conditional expectations preserve L1 convergence. Exercise statements were read; their solutions were not claimed as read.

candidate_scope: Theorem 2.5 proves an isomorphism in Cameron–Martin Hilbert topologies. title: Large Deviations of Continuous Regular Conditional Probabilities
version: Official Open Access Springer published PDF, Journal of Theoretical Probability 31 (2018), 1058–1096; online publication 2016-12-27. The related arXiv v1 is the same work, was not used as read text and is not counted separately.

unproved_interfaces: A target application must establish a good joint LDP and the theorem's exact fiberwise rate and finite normalizing infimum.
The chosen conditional-kernel versions must exist and be weakly continuous on the relevant conditioning-marginal supports; values off support are not determined.
The local conditional numerator/denominator ratio bounds in Theorem 1.2 or 1.3 must be checked; joint weak convergence alone is insufficient.
For the regular-kernel theorem, the observation map must be continuous. The paper does not prove conditional weak convergence under arbitrary parameter changes.
source_formula_flags: Theorem 1.2, physical pp. 4–5: the lower test uses closure of an open ball and the upper test uses W°; preserve both and the support-sequence quantifier.
Theorem 1.3, physical p. 5: the rate is infinite off the conditioning fiber and subtracts the infimum over that fiber.

Example 9.1 density and scaled log-mgf are on physical p. 31 (printed p. 1088); the prose rate sentence is physical p. 32 (printed p. 1089) and prints (x−ry)^2, while the displayed mgf, Legendre transform, and Theorem 1.2 rate give (x−ry)^2/2. The mismatch is isolated.
Example 9.1 prints r≠0, but Z_n over R² is finite only for 1−r²>0. The probability model therefore requires 0<|r|<1 as written; do not use |r|≥1 as a probability density.
